title: Do not lose heart in prayer or neglect almsgiving
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Long record ot-sirach-v7-9 (7:9–33) is titled for 7:9 only; the sayings of 7:10–33 are not itemized.

title: Do not mock someone in bitterness of soul; God humbles and exalts
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not plot lies against brother or friend, or tell any lie
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not babble among elders or repeat words in prayer
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Second half echoes K065 (Matthew 6:5–8, no empty repetition in prayer).

title: Do not hate hard work or farming, created by the Most High
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not join the crowd of sinners; humble your soul greatly
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Never trade a friend for profit or a brother for gold
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not disregard a wise and good wife; her grace surpasses gold
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Treat faithful slaves and workers well; do not withhold a slave’s freedom
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Related but distinct: ot-sirach-v33-31 (33:31–33). 7:21 echoes the release of Hebrew servants (Deuteronomy 15:12).

title: Look after your livestock and keep the animals that serve you
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Discipline your children and bend their necks from youth
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Guard your daughters and give them in marriage to understanding men
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Related: ot-sirach-v26-10 and ot-sirach-v42-11 on watching over daughters; the marriage counsel of 7:25 is unrecorded.

title: Do not divorce a wife you love or trust one you dislike
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Honor your father wholeheartedly and never forget your mother’s birth pains
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: Ben Sira’s own grounds for C0153 (Exodus 20:12); itemized separately like ot-sirach-v3-7.

title: Fear the Lord, honor His priests, and give them their portion
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 7:31 lists the priestly dues of torah-numbers-18-1 (firstfruits, guilt offering, shoulder).

title: Help the poor; show kindness to the living and the dead
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Woe to the sinful nation that has abandoned the Lord
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Prophetic woe, treated as Wisdom like first-pass woes (Isaiah 3:9–11, 5:8–10); 1:5 warns against adding lawlessness.

title: Isaiah contrasts seeking mediums with turning to God
speaker: Isaiah
note: 8:20 completes the contrast: God gave the law as a help against the mediums’ talk (MT: ‘To the law and the testimony!’).

title: The Assyrian envoy challenges Hezekiah’s confidence
speaker: the king of the Assyrians through Rapsakes
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 36:2 records the sending of the envoy that this Commission record describes.

title: Hezekiah’s delegation asks Isaiah to pray for the survivors
speaker: King Hezekiah through Eliakim, Somnas and the priests’ elders
note: Hezekiah sends the delegation (37:2) and its message begins at 37:3; first pass likewise extended 2 Kings 19:4 to 19:3–4.

title: Assyria sends Hezekiah a warning against relying on God
speaker: the king of the Assyrians through messengers
note: The sending of the messengers named in the title is in 37:9.

title: Do not quarrel with your Maker, as clay with its potter
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Saying against disputing the Maker’s purposes (MT: two woes); Paul applies it in Romans 9:20–21, which is not itemized.

title: Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to seek the Lord about Babylon’s attack
speaker: King Zedekiah through Pashhur son of Malchiah and the priest Zephaniah
note: 21:1 records Zedekiah sending the two envoys who carry the request.

title: The priests and false prophets demand a death sentence for Jeremiah
speaker: the priests and false prophets
recipient: Judah’s rulers and all the people
note: Formal charge at Jeremiah’s trial (MT 26:11), like the first-pass demand at 45:4–5. Recording it does not approve it.

title: Judah’s rulers rule that Jeremiah does not deserve death
speaker: Judah’s rulers and all the people
note: Outside candidate list (context verse); the court’s acquittal answering 33:11 (MT 26:16).

title: The elders cite Micah’s case to dissuade the people from killing Jeremiah
speaker: some of the land’s elders
recipient: the whole assembly of the people
note: Counsel from precedent, comparable to Gamaliel’s advice (AUD-48-5-34); MT 26:17–19.

title: Jehoiakim sends men to Egypt to bring back the prophet Uriah
speaker: King Jehoiakim
note: Reported order of a wicked king; Uriah is then executed (MT 26:22–23).

title: Zedekiah’s covenant requires every Hebrew slave to be set free
speaker: King Zedekiah, by covenant with the people
note: Royal covenant of release (MT 34:8–10; also 41:15), distinct from the Torah law God recalls in ot-jeremiah-v41-14.

title: Jehoiakim sends Jehudi to fetch the scroll and read it to him
speaker: King Jehoiakim
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported royal order (MT 36:21); the officials’ earlier summons of Baruch (43:14–16) is a first-pass finding.

title: Elnathan, Gedaliah and Gemariah urge the king not to burn the scroll
speaker: Elnathan, Gedaliah and Gemariah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list (context verse); a reported request the king ignored (MT 36:25).

title: Jehoiakim orders Baruch and Jeremiah arrested
speaker: King Jehoiakim
recipient: Jerahmeel the king’s son and Seraiah son of Azriel
note: Explicit reported order (MT 36:26); the officials’ warning to hide is ot-jeremiah-v43-19.

title: Babylon’s commanders release Jeremiah from prison into Gedaliah’s care
speaker: the king of Babylon’s commanders
recipient: their men and Gedaliah son of Ahikam
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported order (‘they sent and took Jeremiah’); the Greek omits MT 39:4–13. The later release is ot-jeremiah-v47-5.

title: Babylon’s king appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah
speaker: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Also 47:5, 47:11, 48:2, 48:10, 48:18. Same appointment as first-pass 2 Kings 25:22 (B08 P00956); merge as one record.

title: Baalis king of Ammon sends Ishmael to assassinate Gedaliah
speaker: Baalis (Belisa) king of the Ammonites
note: Reported in the commanders’ warning, which Gedaliah disbelieves (MT 40:14); Johanan’s follow-up request is ot-jeremiah-v47-15.

title: Ishmael lures the mourning pilgrims in to Gedaliah to kill them
speaker: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
recipient: eighty pilgrims from Shechem, Salem and Samaria
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Deceitful invitation (‘Come in to Gedaliah’) before the massacre (MT 41:6–7).

title: Ezekiel announces judgment to the mountains and valleys of Israel
speaker: the Lord
note: 6:2 holds the charge itself: ‘set your face firmly against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them’.

title: Ezekiel is told to look north and see the people’s lawlessness
speaker: the Lord (in the vision)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: First order of the temple vision tour, like ot-ezekiel-v8-9; 8:6 adds ‘you will yet see greater lawlessness’.

title: Ezekiel is told to enter and see the people’s wrongdoing
speaker: the Lord (in the vision)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: ‘Son of man, dig’ (8:8) opens the way for ‘Go in and see’; one continuous order.

title: Judgment in the vision begins at the sanctuary and spares the marked
speaker: the Lord (in the vision)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 9:7 completes the order: defile the house, fill the roads with the dead, go out and strike. Long record AUD-30-9-3 omits it.

title: Ezekiel is told to testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness
speaker: the Lord
note: 16:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v16-3); compare the first-pass extension of ot-ezekiel-v22-3 to 22:2.

title: God recalls Israel rejecting His ordinances in the wilderness
speaker: the Lord
note: 20:11 recalls giving the commands by which a person lives (Leviticus 18:5), which 20:13 says Israel rejected; 20:12 parallels ot-ezekiel-v20-20.

title: The exiles ask Ezekiel to explain his refusal to mourn
speaker: the people in exile
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list (context verse); the request is answered by the oracle recorded at 24:21 (ot-ezekiel-v24-21).

summary: Most of the 171 passages need nothing; the gaps are 16 unitemized sayings inside the long Sirach 7:9–33 record, Zedekiah's release covenant, reported royal orders and the trial in Jeremiah, and the prophet's commissions and vision commands in Ezekiel.
